copper complexes of 8-hyroxyquinolines and dithiocarbamates are novel proteasome inhibitors, and apoptosis inducers that are preferentially active in cancer cells, but not in normal cells, and that these effects are dependent on copper in the cells.
copper-containing compounds can induce apoptosis in cancer cells, while they are non-toxic in non-transformed cells.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of copper-containing compounds that target breast cancer cells by inducing apoptosis through proteasome inhibition.
the role of copper in breast cancer cells and its potential as a therapeutic target.
the development of novel cancer-specific proteasomal inhibitors and apoptosis inducer.

the feature of breast cancer tissues and cells to accumulate copper can potentially be exploited as a targeting method in anticancer therapy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

copper is an important element in the development of cancer, and copper chelating agents can be used as anticancer drugs, especially when used in combination with other drugs that have copper chelating activity.
copper accumulation in tumor cells and tissues, which is common in many tumors, can be used as an approach for cancer treatment through the use of copper chelating drugs.
copper is an essential element for tumor growth and development, and copper-targeted therapy is a potential approach for the treatment of human breast cancer.
